job.question: What does the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0 ask about GP-led secondaries and continuation funds in Section 6?
job.expected_facts: Section 6.0 opens with two Yes/No screening questions. 6.1 asks whether the Firm has done a GP-led secondary in the last five years, and 6.2 asks the same for a continuation fund transaction. Each has four follow-ups: did the LPAC review conflicts in every transaction; was a status quo option available to existing LPs in every transaction; was GP carry rolled over at 100% in every transaction; and were portfolio companies in an IPO or pre-IPO process excluded. Narrative questions 6.3-6.11 then cover: how conflicts of interest are reviewed with the LPAC and LPs (timing, information, Firm benefits not accruing to LPs, transparency on LPAC members or affiliates acting as acquirers); the information given to the LPAC/LPs and its timing; how new fund documents and side letters are structured; the options offered to LPs, including status quo, and differences for new or 'rolling' LPs; the impact on GP economics, alignment of interests and Key Person provisions; the rationale for this route rather than a fund extension or traditional exit; how the bidding universe and valuations are set (secondary managers, third-party advisers, valuation providers); fee structuring (broken deal/termination fees, sharing of transaction costs, management fee, carry); and disclosure of related deals between the GP and acquirers (e.g. stapled transactions or side deals).
job.acceptance: Accept a concise summary covering transaction history, four screening follow-ups, conflicts/disclosure and information, legal/economic/LP options, rationale, bidding/valuation, fees/carry and related deals. Exact subquestion numbering and every illustrative detail are optional.

reviews.reason: The supplied document is a Los Angeles Fire and Police Pensions RFP for financial statement audit services, not the ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0. Its Section 6 is an appendix and does not address GP-led secondaries or continuation funds.
